samples.summary: Crop test asserts only `isCropping() === false`, which holds for `exitImageCrop(true)` too — the "discarded rather than committed" claim in its own comment is not asserted
samples.evidence: The heal calls `exitImageCrop(false)` (editor.ts:1568) and the test comment at line 378-379 says the session "is discarded rather than committed". But the assertions are `isCropping()` false and `getCurrentSlideId()`. `finishCropSession()` runs in a `finally` for both `commit` values (editor.ts:2466-2479), so `isCropping()` is false either way. The sibling text-edit test (line 300) does the right thing — it asserts through `store.undo()` restoring the slides, which is what distinguishes a `store.batch()` write from none. The crop test has no equivalent undo-stack assertion, so a future flip of `exitImageCrop(false)` → `(true)` is only caught incidentally (by `commitCropFrame`'s `updateElementFrame` throwing 'Slide not found' out of `render()`), not by the assertion the test claims to make.

samples.summary: The heal's `setCellSelection(null)` (table cell selection anchored to the removed slide) has no test
samples.evidence: `resolveCurrentSlide` clears cell selection at editor.ts:1570, alongside `selection.clear()` (which IS covered by the 'drops the selection carried on the removed slide' test at line 225). No test in the new file — or elsewhere — enters a table cell selection and then removes the slide; removing the `setCellSelection(null)` line would leave every test green.

samples.summary: No test exercises the heal with a stale `currentIndex` — `setCurrentSlide` never updates it, yet every test renders between the cursor move and the removal
samples.evidence: `currentIndex` is only assigned inside `resolveCurrentSlide` (editor.ts:1543, 1562); `setCurrentSlide` (editor.ts:1507-1517) does not touch it. So a `setCurrentSlide(last)` followed by a removal with no intervening resolve would heal off the stale index (0). Every test in the file either calls `frame(ed)` right after `setCurrentSlide` (lines 152, 178, 204, 217, 238, 257, 290, 324, 391) or calls `enterTextEditing`/`enterImageCrop`, which render internally — so this path is never covered, and a heal landing on the wrong slide there would go unnoticed.
searchedFor: read the whole new test file

samples.summary: Nothing asserts the #883 symptom itself — that the healed slide actually paints (the heal's `renderer.markDirty()` is untested)
samples.evidence: The issue quoted in the file header is 'nothing would paint'. Every test asserts only `getCurrentSlideId()` / `getSelection()` / `isTextEditing()`. The heal calls `this.renderer.markDirty()` (editor.ts:1561) so the canvas re-paints on the same frame that healed; deleting that line would keep the whole suite green while leaving the user with the stale/blank canvas the issue is about. Other slides suites do assert paint output (e.g. via the canvas test env), so a render-side assertion is available.
searchedFor: grep markDirty in editor.ts heal block

samples.summary: 'clamps to the first slide when the deck head is removed' uses 2 slides, so only one slide remains and the test cannot distinguish 'previous' from 'first' from 'any surviving slide'
samples.evidence: setup(2), remove slideIds[0] → the deck holds exactly one slide, so `expect(getCurrentSlideId()).toBe(slideIds[1])` passes for any policy that lands on a surviving slide (it only rules out an unclamped `slides[-1] === undefined`). The suite already shows awareness of this class of problem in the comment at lines 249-253; the same reasoning argues for setup(3) here so the clamp target is a genuine choice among survivors.

finding.summary: 'settles after one heal and stays on the healed slide' is vacuous — it cannot fail even if the heal re-runs every frame
finding.evidence: The test sets up 2 slides, makes slideIds[1] current (index 1) and removes it, then asserts after 3 frames that the cursor is slideIds[0]. `resolveCurrentSlide` computes `nextIdx = Math.min(Math.max(this.currentIndex - 1, 0), len - 1)` (editor.ts:1534) which floors at 0, and after the heal the deck holds exactly one slide. So even a hypothetically broken implementation that healed on every frame and walked the cursor backwards each time would still land on slideIds[0] — the stated claim ('repeated frames must not keep walking the cursor backwards') is untestable in this configuration. It would need e.g. 3+ slides with the cursor healed to a non-zero index (start at index 2, remove it, assert it stays at index 1 over repeated frames).

verdict.reason: The test as described does not exist. The finding says 'settles after one heal and stays on the healed slide' uses 2 slides with the cursor on slideIds[1] and asserts slideIds[0], making the assertion pinned by the Math.max(...,0) floor. The actual test (current-slide-heal.test.ts:248-262) calls setup(3), sets the current slide to slideIds[2], removes it, runs 3 frames and asserts slideIds[1] — exactly the 3-slide / non-zero-index configuration the finding itself says would be required. Against the real implementation (editor.ts:1552-1562), a heal that re-ran each frame would recompute Math.min(Math.max(1-1,0), 1) = 0 and move the cursor to slideIds[0], failing the assertion, so the test does discriminate the behavior it claims. The test's own comment at lines 249-253 documents rejecting the 2-slide setup for precisely the reason the finding raises. Grep confirms only one test with this title in the repo, so there is no other variant matching the description. The finding's line citation for nextIdx (editor.ts:1534) is also off; the actual line is 1554.
